doc: What Limen checks in its own repository, and which of it the consumer-facing `limen verify` also checks. Every repository check script and every rule identifier the boundary guardrails can emit is listed here, either as `consumer` (the CLI enforces it, from the same source) or as `repositoryOnly` with the reason it cannot or should not apply to a consumer. test/boundary-rules.test.ts fails when a check script, a TypeScript-subset rule, a layer rule or a boundary rule exists that is not classified here, or when an entry names something that no longer exists — so the consumer verify cannot silently fall behind Limen's own checks again. Guardrail-owned.

boundaryRules.doc: The engine-authority rule set. Consumer and repository run the same file (architecture/boundary-rules.json) through two implementations held to the same fixtures (test/fixtures/boundary-rules/cases.json).

verdicts.doc: Repository and consumer both refuse a boundary that checks nothing: the CLI reports `not-configured` (LIMEN012, exit 8); scripts/check-architecture.ts fails when limen.config.json declares no engine path.

check-architecture.ts.consumerParts: the engine-authority boundary over limen.config.json paths (boundary-rules.json)
check-architecture.ts.repositoryOnlyParts: default-deny coverage of src/ and site/app, the engine-project and WASM host-shim manifests (architecture/wasm-hosts.json), and the Core manifest (architecture/core.json)
check-architecture.ts.reason: Coverage, host-shim and Core rules describe this repository's own layout and package; a consumer declares only engine and kernel paths, and has no Core.

check-layers.ts.reason: Import directions between Limen's own layers (architecture/layers.json), its zero-dependency package rule and the browser-type ban in its own contract. A consumer's module graph is its own architecture, not Limen's; the engine-authority part that used to live here moved to boundary-rules.json and is shared.

check-typescript.ts.reason: The restricted TypeScript subset is a type-aware analysis on the TypeScript compiler API. The CLI is a self-contained, trimmed .NET binary with no TypeScript compiler; its lexical engine-dynamic-type (`any`) and escape-hatch (`eval`) rules are the part that can be shipped.

check-docs.ts.reason: Limen's own documentation and learning path.

check-views.ts.reason: Limen's own example and site view contracts.

check-scope.ts.reason: ROS work-item path scope for Limen's own commits; consumers run ROS themselves.

repositoryOnlyRules.doc: Rule identifiers emitted by Limen's repository guardrails that the CLI does not emit, each with its reason.

typescript.reason: Type-aware rules of the restricted TypeScript subset (check-typescript.ts); they need the TypeScript compiler. any-type and script-execution have lexical counterparts the CLI does ship (engine-dynamic-type, escape-hatch).

layers.reason: Limen's own layer map and contract (check-layers.ts).
